root_idea.summary: The root combines the ideas of adhesion, persistent attachment, and admiration at beauty. Its lexical field includes both physical sticking and the figurative fixing of attention, desire, or hostility.
root_idea.development: Physical adhesive action develops into clinging and fondness, then into causing someone or something to become attached or directed toward another. A parallel branch concerns beauty, wonder, and goodliness; persistent attachment also appears in uninterrupted weeping.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form IV verb, normalized to its Classical Arabic perfect-tense citation form أَغْرَى.

senses.definition: To induce, incite, or set someone toward a person or thing; to make someone attached or eagerly directed toward it.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with a directed object, often with بِـ. In the Quran, the hostile construction means setting someone upon others or granting him mastery over them.

senses.definition: To cause enmity and hatred to arise and become fixed between parties, thereby producing discord or strife.
senses.usage_conditions: The construction أَغْرَى بَيْنَهُمْ الْعَدَاوَةَ وَالْبَغْضَاءَ treats enmity and hatred as something caused to adhere between them; غَرَاةٌ denotes the resulting excitation of disorder.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To glue or make one thing adhere to another, including gluing feathers onto an arrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical adhesive action; the adhesive itself is غِرَاءٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To adhere, cling, or stick to something; an adhering substance may cover it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of physical adherence and figurative clinging. Lane illustrates it with fat adhering to and covering the heart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become attached to, fond of, or eagerly desirous of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This denotes self-motivated attachment or infatuation, without another person inciting it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To persist or persevere in anger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic use describing continued anger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water, to become cold or cool.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported of water in a pool or watercourse; the lexical sources differ over the precise term for the water body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wonder or be amazed; لَا غَرْوَ means “there is no wonder” or “it is not surprising.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The phrase لَا غَرْوَ is a conventional expression of unsurprise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To daub, smear, or rub something over; hence, to be daubed or smeared.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially associated with applying an adhesive or coating substance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To continue without interruption; of the eye, to persist in weeping and overflow with tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression غَارَتِ الْعَيْنُ بِالْبُكَاءِ describes uninterrupted or copious weeping.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wrangle, quarrel, or contend with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form VI expression is reported specifically of mutual wrangling in anger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make or render a thing goodly or beautiful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical Arabic Form IV usage distinct from the Quranic incitement constructions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The afterbirth or tissue descending from the womb with the child.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A young or newly born animal, especially a young bovine or camel; more broadly, a newborn before its flesh becomes firm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources vary over whether the bovine reference is specifically to the wild cow; the broader youngling sense is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Extremely lean, meagre, or emaciated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or figurative extension from the soft, undeveloped condition of a young animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Goodliness or beauty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun denoting the quality of being goodly or beautiful.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state of attachment, fondness, or eager preoccupation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun or verbal noun associated with غَرِيَ بِهِ and attachment to something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Glue or another adhesive substance used to make things adhere; also a substance used for smearing or coating.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources describe adhesives made from fish or skins and related mucilaginous substances.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who has no beast of burden to carry him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal expression, رَجُلٌ غِرَاءٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Made to adhere; adherent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival or passive description of something fixed or attached.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Goodly or beautiful, especially in appearance; also applied to a beautiful person, thing, or building.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources particularly mention beauty of face and goodly buildings, while also extending the adjective to other things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular idol or object of pagan worship on which sacrifices were made and with whose blood a person was smeared.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized cultural and religious usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A red dye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized material noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Froth or foam.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a form apparently produced by transposition from رُغَاوَى; the form is marked as nonstandard or uncertain in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Made attached or fond of something; made eagerly preoccupied with it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial expression derived from أَغْرَى بِهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Glued or made to adhere.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The passive participle may describe an object fixed with adhesive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A feathered arrow, literally an arrow whose feathers have been glued on; by the same construction, a glued bow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional lexical use of the passive participle in descriptions of arrows and bows.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Proper-name and cultural referent, not an independent lexical meaning.

cautions: The internal QAC lemma أَغْرَيْ is normalized to the dictionary citation form أَغْرَى.
The form غُرَاوَى meaning “froth” is explicitly reported as an apparent transposition and should be treated as lexically uncertain.
The cooling sense is reported with variant descriptions of the relevant pool or watercourse term.
